# Mean branch length per region and type (domesticate vs wild)
Plot within group mean
```{r}
to_plot_long <- plot_data %>%
  select(-comparison) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(branch_len_wild, branch_len_dom),
               names_to = "status", values_to = "branch_len") %>%
  mutate(status = recode(status,
                          branch_len_wild = "wild",
                          branch_len_dom  = "domesticate"))

plot1 <- ggplot(to_plot_long, aes(x = region, y = log(branch_len), fill = status)) +
  geom_violin()+
  theme_bw()+ 
  labs(y="log(branch length)")+
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust=1))+
  scale_fill_manual(values = unname(khroma::color("bright")(7))[c(5, 6)])+
  labs(x="Continent", fill="type",title="Mean branch length per region and pig type",subtitle = "bar represents within group mean")+
  stat_summary(
    fun = mean,
    geom = "crossbar",
    aes(group = status),
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.9),
    width = 0.8,
    color = "red",
    linewidth = 0.4,
    show.legend = FALSE
  )

plot2 <- ggplot(to_plot_long, aes(x = region, y = branch_len, fill = status)) +
  geom_violin()+
  theme_bw()+ 
  labs(y="branch length")+
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust=1))

plot1
plot2

  ggsave(
    filename = paste0("for_paper_plots/mean_per_group_logged.png"),
    plot = plot1,
    width = 6,
    height = 4.5,
    limitsize = FALSE,
    create.dir = TRUE)
```

# Wilcox test within each region (wild vs. domesticate, is there a sig. difference in branch length?)
wilcox test (paired) to test within each region, if there is a difference between the wild and the domesticate
```{r}
asia   <- plot_data %>% filter(region == "Asia")
europe <- plot_data %>% filter(region == "Europe")

wilcox.test(asia$branch_len_wild,   asia$branch_len_dom,   paired = TRUE)
wilcox.test(europe$branch_len_wild, europe$branch_len_dom, paired = TRUE)

mean(asia$branch_length_diff)
mean(europe$branch_length_diff)

mean(asia$branch_len_wild)
mean(asia$branch_len_dom)
mean(europe$branch_len_wild)
mean(europe$branch_len_dom)
```
In both cases, the branch length is significantly higher in the wild than in the domesticate. Confirm this by simply checking the mean per each group. The difference is more pronounced in Asia than in Europe

# Plots by gene 
## Chromosome
Plot by each gene. Now, instead of collapsing we want each gene as a single point, to see if there is a pattern between the genes affected by domestication in Asia and in Europe. Also, now our measure of interest is the log of the ratio between the wild and domesticate branch lenght. This is nice, because the log will be positive with the wild > domesticate, and negative when the wild < domesticate. Plot by chromosome. 

Also, plot both the scatter plot and the rank of the genes, as a bar plot. Color them chromosome, to see if there is a chromosome that is contributing significantly to the pattern.
```{r}
plot_data_summary <- plot_data %>%
  select(-c(branch_len_wild, branch_len_dom)) %>%
  group_by(gene, region, chromosome) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_branch_length_ratio      = mean(branch_length_ratio, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_branch_length_difference = mean(branch_length_diff, na.rm = TRUE),
    n      = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      chromosome = as.numeric(str_split_i(chromosome, "_", 2)),
      chromosome = factor(chromosome, levels = sort(unique(chromosome))))

plot_data_summary_wide <- plot_data_summary %>% pivot_wider(names_from  = region,
                                                    values_from = c(mean_branch_length_ratio, mean_branch_length_difference, n)) %>% drop_na() %>%
  mutate(n=n_Europe+n_Asia,
         log_eu   = log(mean_branch_length_ratio_Europe),
         log_asia = log(mean_branch_length_ratio_Asia),
         quadrant = case_when(
           log_eu >  0 & log_asia >  0 ~ "Both Asia and Europe wild > domesticate",
           log_eu <= 0 & log_asia >  0 ~ "Asia only wild > domesticate",
           log_eu >  0 & log_asia <= 0 ~ "Europe only wild > domesticate",
           log_eu <= 0 & log_asia <= 0 ~ "Both Asia and Europe wild < domesticate"))

chrom_cols <- setNames(
  colour("discrete rainbow")(nlevels(plot_data_summary$chromosome)),
  levels(plot_data_summary$chromosome)
)

p_quad <- ggplot(plot_data_summary_wide, aes(x=log(mean_branch_length_ratio_Europe), y=log(mean_branch_length_ratio_Asia), color = chromosome))+
  geom_point()+
  theme_bw()+
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0)+
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0)+
  scale_color_manual(values = chrom_cols)

p_col <- ggplot(plot_data_summary,
       aes(x = reorder_within(gene, -mean_branch_length_ratio, region),
           y = log(mean_branch_length_ratio),
           fill = chromosome, color = chromosome)) +
  geom_col(width = 1, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0) +
  facet_wrap(~region, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_x_reordered() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = chrom_cols) +
  scale_color_manual(values = chrom_cols) +
  labs(x = "Genes (ranked within region)") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.x = element_blank())

p_col_by_chrom <- plot_data_summary %>%
  mutate(panel = paste(region, chromosome)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder_within(gene, -mean_branch_length_ratio, panel),
             y = log(mean_branch_length_ratio),
             fill = chromosome, color = chromosome)) +
  geom_col(width = 1, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0) +
  facet_wrap(region ~ chromosome, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_x_reordered() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = chrom_cols) +
  scale_color_manual(values = chrom_cols) +
  labs(x = "Genes (ranked within panel)") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "none")

ggsave(
    filename = paste0("plots/by_chromosome/quad_scatter.jpg"),
    plot = p_quad,
    width = 8,
    height = 4.5,
    limitsize = FALSE)

ggsave(
    filename = paste0("plots/by_chromosome/bar_rank.jpg"),
    plot = p_col,
    width = 12, height = 5, dpi = 300, limitsize = FALSE)

ggsave(
    filename = paste0("plots/by_chromosome/bar_rank_chrom.jpg"),
    plot = p_col_by_chrom,
    width = 12, height = 8, dpi = 300, limitsize = FALSE)

p_quad
p_col
p_col_by_chrom
```
Quadrant plot is interesting (we'll come back to that later.) Chromosome is difficult to interpret.

# KW test for chromosome, family in each reiong (including post hoc Dunn/ wilcox tests)

Like the chromosome results, difficult to interpret the plots. We can do a KW to test whether or not there is a statistical difference between families, as well as chromosomes. Using slightly different datasets for both because there are some genes for which we have chromosome information but no family information.

```{r}
europe_gene_family <- plot_data_summary_gene_family %>% filter(region=="Europe")
asia_gene_family <-   plot_data_summary_gene_family %>% filter(region=="Asia")

europe_length <-      plot_data_summary %>% filter(region == "Europe")
asia_length <-        plot_data_summary %>% filter(region == "Asia")
```

Europe KW tests:
```{r}
KW_family_eur = kruskal.test(mean_branch_length_ratio ~ Family,
                    data = europe_gene_family)
print(KW_family_eur)

KW_chrom_Europe = kruskal.test(mean_branch_length_ratio ~ chromosome,
                    data = europe_length)
print(KW_chrom_Europe)
```
NO significant result for Europe, for either chromosome or family.

```{r}
KW_family_asia = kruskal.test(mean_branch_length_ratio ~ Family,
                    data = asia_gene_family)
print(KW_family_asia)

KW_chrom_aisa = kruskal.test(mean_branch_length_ratio ~ chromosome,
                    data = asia_length)
print(KW_chrom_aisa)
```
In Asia, we do see a significant result for both family and chromosome.

Post hoc: both dunn and wilcox 
```{r}
dunn.test(asia_length$mean_branch_length_ratio, 
          asia_length$chromosome,
          method="bonferroni",
          kw=TRUE)

pairwise.wilcox.test(asia_length$mean_branch_length_ratio,
                     asia_length$chromosome, p.adjust.method = 'bonf')
```

Asia: diff between chromosomes 7 and 9?

```{r}
dunn.test(asia_gene_family$mean_branch_length_ratio, 
          asia_gene_family$Family,
          method="bonferroni",
          kw=TRUE)

pairwise.wilcox.test(asia_gene_family$mean_branch_length_ratio,
                     asia_gene_family$Family, p.adjust.method = 'bonf')
```
Asia: significant difference between families 4 and 7

**** both the Dunn and Wilcox test show the same thing. The dunn is perhaps slightly more appropriate as the standard post hoc KW?

# Regression through the origin on gene scatterplot

Figures for paper version 1:

Going back to our quadrant plot, we want to add a linear regression. Null hypothesis is slope=0, meaning points randomly scatter around the origin. Alternative hypothesis: there is a linear relationship between the genes that are domesticated in Europe and in Asia. That is to say, that knowing something about the relationship between the wild and the domesticate branch lenght in Europe predicts something about that same relationship in Aisa.

OPTIONAL non-origin forced model
```{r}
model <- lm(log(mean_branch_length_ratio_Asia) ~ log(mean_branch_length_ratio_Europe), data = plot_data_summary_wide)
summary(model)
sigma(model)
summary(model)$r.squared
```

Now, for the model through the origin

```{r}
model_origin <- lm(log(mean_branch_length_ratio_Asia) ~ 0 + log(mean_branch_length_ratio_Europe), data = plot_data_summary_wide)
summary(model_origin)
r2 <- summary(model_origin)$r.squared
p  <- summary(model_origin)$coefficients[1, 4]
```

To add the predictive line to the plot
```{r}
predicted_df <- data.frame(asia_pred = predict(model_origin, plot_data_summary_wide), mean_branch_length_ratio_Europe=log(plot_data_summary_wide$mean_branch_length_ratio_Europe))
```

```{r}
lab <- paste0("R² = ", signif(r2, 3), "\n",
              "p = ", format(signif(p, 3), scientific = TRUE))


scatted_regression <- ggplot(data = plot_data_summary_wide, aes(x = log(mean_branch_length_ratio_Europe), y = log(mean_branch_length_ratio_Asia), color=quadrant)) + 
  geom_point() +
  geom_line(color='red',data = predicted_df, aes(x=mean_branch_length_ratio_Europe, y=asia_pred))+
  theme_bw()+
  theme(legend.position="bottom")+
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0)+
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0)+
  labs(x="Europe: log(wild bl /domesticate bl)",y="Asia: log(wild bl /domesticate bl)", title = "Branch length ratio by gene and continent", subtitle = "linear model forced through the origin", color="")+
  annotate("text", x = -Inf, y = Inf, hjust = -0.1, vjust = 1.5,
           label = lab, size = 3)+
  scale_color_mediumcontrast(guide = guide_legend(nrow = 2))

ggsave(
  filename = paste0("for_paper_plots/scatter_regression.png"),
  plot = scatted_regression,
  width = 6,
  height = 6,
  limitsize = FALSE)
  
```
